skill.name: personwise-developer-quickstart
skill.description: Creates grounded developer quickstart courses from supplied API documentation, SDK guides, and reference materials through the PersonWise course workflow.
skill.summary: Turn verified developer documentation into an interactive course for a first successful API call.
skill.author: personwiseai

security_audit.summary: The 142 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, routine installer checks, fixed release URLs, and signed descriptor data. A high-confidence semantic finding remains because the skill directs quiet installation of a downloaded third-party CLI without separate informed confirmation.

remediation.issue: First-time CLI installation lacks explicit informed confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Before downloading, show the CLI version, release origin, install path, and executable purpose. Require explicit user confirmation independent of the course request.

content.user_title: Build a Grounded Developer Quickstart Course
content.value_statement: Developers need a reliable path from credentials to a first API call. This skill turns supplied technical sources into a grounded interactive course.
actual_capabilities: Builds a developer quickstart course from supplied API documentation and SDK guides.
Preserves verified endpoints, parameters, versions, and code examples from source materials.
Creates and monitors durable PersonWise course runs through review checkpoints.
Uploads user-selected source documents and tracks processing status.
Reviews outlines, scripts, images, access state, and final playability.
limitations: Requires PersonWise CLI 1.1.6 or newer, browser OAuth, and available course credits.
Cannot verify claims that are absent from the supplied technical sources.
Does not create full API reference documentation or internal team onboarding.
Course size and publication options depend on current account limits and permissions.

use_cases.title: Launch an API Quickstart
use_cases.description: Convert product API documentation into a course that guides developers to one verified successful request.

use_cases.title: Teach an SDK Setup
use_cases.description: Turn SDK installation and authentication guides into a structured learning sequence with grounded examples.

use_cases.title: Prepare Customer Enablement
use_cases.description: Create a private technical adoption course from approved customer documentation and reference files.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Quickstart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a private developer quickstart from these API documents. Guide learners from credentials to their first successful call.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a focused course from supplied documentation.

prompt_templates.prompt: Build a six-page SDK tutorial from the attached guides. Preserve every verified command and explain the successful response.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs structured SDK adoption training.

prompt_templates.prompt: Create a materials-only course from the selected files. State the documented version and exclude every unsupported claim.
prompt_templates.scenario: A regulated team requires strict source grounding.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing course for factual support and progression. Correct objective issues, enable requested link access, and report final playability evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs review, controlled revision, and publication.

output_examples.input: Create a private quickstart from our authentication and first-request guides.
output: Resolved course: five pages covering setup, authentication, the first request, response reading, and next steps.
All technical details were grounded in the selected guides.
The course is playable through a private, sign-in-required link.

output_examples.input: Turn the attached SDK guide into a link-access tutorial.
output: Created a six-page SDK tutorial using the documented version and verified examples.
Source processing and course review completed successfully.
Link access is enabled, and the returned share link is playable.

best_practices: Supply current API documentation, SDK guides, and exact reference files.
State the target learner, desired outcome, page count, language, and access mode.
Review generated technical claims against the cited source version before publication.
anti_patterns: Do not request undocumented endpoints, parameters, authentication methods, or security guarantees.
Do not use this skill as a replacement for complete API reference documentation.
Do not upload files that the user did not select without explicit approval.

faq.question: What sources should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide current API documentation, SDK guides, authentication instructions, and reference materials that support the course.

faq.question: Will the skill invent missing code?
faq.answer: No. It must preserve verifiable code and exclude unsupported endpoints, parameters, versions, or authentication details.

faq.question: Can it create a full API reference?
faq.answer: No. It creates a focused quickstart course that leads to a first successful API call.

faq.question: Does it require a PersonWise account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires browser OAuth, a compatible PersonWise CLI, and sufficient account credits.

faq.question: What access mode does it use?
faq.answer: Private access is the default. Link access or publication is used only when the request specifies a broader target.

faq.question: Can it update an existing course?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review and refine supported fields while preserving course order and current state.
